hints: Find the five key summary statistics for the 55 ordered values: minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, and maximum.
For $n = 55$, the median is the $\frac{55 + 1}{2} = 28$th value, the lower quartile is the $\frac{55 + 1}{4} = 14$th value, and the upper quartile is the $\frac{3(55 + 1)}{4} = 42$nd value.
Read these values from the list: Minimum $= 5$, $Q_1 = 18$, Median $= 25$, $Q_3 = 50$, Maximum $= 70$.
Draw the box between $Q_1 = 18$ and $Q_3 = 50$, mark the median at $25$, and extend whiskers to $5$ and $70$ on a clearly labelled linear scale.
walkthrough:
Identify the five-number summary from the ordered list of $n = 55$ values:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Minimum} &= 5 \\ Q_1 &= \text{14th value} = 18 \\ \text{Median } (Q_2) &= \text{28th value} = 25 \\ Q_3 &= \text{42nd value} = 50 \\ \text{Maximum} &= 70 \end{aligned}$$

Construct the box-and-whisker plot on a linear scale labelled 'Distance (km)':
- Draw a rectangular box spanning from lower quartile $18$ to upper quartile $50$.
- Draw a vertical line segment inside the box at median $25$.
- Draw whiskers extending from the box ends to the minimum $5$ and maximum $70$.
teacher_walkthrough: A box-and-whisker plot visually summarizes a data set using five key values: the minimum, the lower quartile ($Q_1$), the median ($Q_2$), the upper quartile ($Q_3$), and the maximum.

Step 1: Determine the positions of the quartiles and median for $n = 55$ values:
- Minimum value: the smallest number in the list is $5$.
- Lower quartile position: $\frac{n + 1}{4} = \frac{55 + 1}{4} = 14$th value. Counting to the 14th value gives $Q_1 = 18$.
- Median position: $\frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{55 + 1}{2} = 28$th value. Counting to the 28th value gives $Q_2 = 25$.
- Upper quartile position: $\frac{3(n + 1)}{4} = \frac{3(56)}{4} = 42$nd value. Counting to the 42nd value gives $Q_3 = 50$.
- Maximum value: the largest number in the list is $70$.

Step 2: Draw the plot on a uniform linear horizontal scale starting at 0 and extending to at least 70, with appropriate axis label 'Distance travelled (km)':
- Draw vertical lines at $18$, $25$, and $50$.
- Form a box from $18$ to $50$, divided by the median line at $25$.
- Draw horizontal whiskers extending from $18$ down to $5$ and from $50$ up to $70$, capped with neat end bars.

hints: Recall the standard outlier boundaries: below $Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR$ or above $Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR$.
Calculate the interquartile range: $IQR = Q_3 - Q_1 = 50 - 18 = 32$.
Check both boundaries against the minimum ($5$) and maximum ($70$) data values to confirm no data points fall outside.
walkthrough:
Calculate the interquartile range ($IQR$) and the outlier margin:
$$\begin{aligned} IQR &= Q_3 - Q_1 = 50 - 18 = 32 \\ 1.5 \times IQR &= 1.5 \times 32 = 48 \end{aligned}$$

Determine the lower and upper outlier thresholds:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Lower threshold} &= Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR = 18 - 48 = -30 \\ \text{Upper threshold} &= Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR = 50 + 48 = 98 \end{aligned}$$

Compare the data range $[5, 70]$ to these thresholds:
$$\text{Since } \text{Minimum } 5 > -30 \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Maximum } 70 < 98,$$
All data points lie strictly within the non-outlier limits $[-30, 98]$, so there are no outliers.
teacher_walkthrough: To test whether any observation in a data set is an outlier, we use the standard $1.5 \times IQR$ rule.

Step 1: Calculate the Interquartile Range ($IQR$):
$$IQR = Q_3 - Q_1 = 50 - 18 = 32$$

Step 3: Establish the lower and upper outlier fences:
- Lower boundary: $Q_1 - 1.5 \times IQR = 18 - 48 = -30$
- Upper boundary: $Q_3 + 1.5 \times IQR = 50 + 48 = 98$

Step 4: Compare the data endpoints to the fences:
- The lowest value in the survey is $5$, which is well above the lower fence of $-30$ ($5 > -30$).
- The highest value in the survey is $70$, which is well below the upper fence of $98$ ($70 < 98$).
Because every single value in the dataset falls within the interval $[-30, 98]$, there are no outliers.
